message.content:
Driving from San Francisco to Los Angeles is roughly 380–400 miles (about 610–640 km) along the I‑5 corridor. Under normal conditions—steady traffic, no major detours, and staying within speed limits—you can expect the trip to take around **6 hours**.  

If you’re heading out during rush hour or on a weekend when traffic tends to be heavier, add an extra hour or two. Conversely, if you’re traveling on a clear day with minimal stops, you might squeeze it into about **5½ hours**.  

A quick way to plan is to use a navigation app (Google Maps, Waze, Apple Maps) which will give you real‑time traffic estimates and suggest alternate routes if needed.
